blocks.caption: Outline from Natural Earth (public domain); modern coastlines and borders.

questions.q: Where is the source of a river usually?
questions.a: On high land, such as hills or mountains
questions.model: Rivers flow downhill. So they must start high up. The source is on high land.

questions.q: Which sea does the Thames flow into?

questions.a: A smaller river that joins a bigger one

questions.q: Core: On your UK map from last lesson, draw and label the Severn, Thames, Trent and Tay with arrows showing the flow.
questions.a: Severn from mid-Wales to the Bristol Channel; Thames from the Cotswolds east through London; Trent north to the Humber; Tay east to the North Sea
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: blue line from the Cotswolds through London to the sea, arrow pointing east, label 'Thames'.

questions.q: Extend: Label the source and mouth of the Thames.
questions.a: Source in the Cotswolds (Gloucestershire); mouth at the Thames Estuary into the North Sea

questions.q: Stretch: Why do UK rivers starting in the west often flow east?
questions.a: The high land is in the west, so water flows downhill to the lower east and the sea

questions.q: Where a river meets the sea is the:
Big question: where does a river begin, and where does it end?
questions.a: At a source on high land, and at a mouth where it meets the sea or a lake
